---
# The landing page. Formerly index.html, a hand-written page that
# rmarkdown::render_site() copied into docs/ untouched -- which meant it had to
# carry its own copy of the navbar and of the footer partial, and load
# Bootstrap 3, jQuery and Font Awesome out of site_libs/ to make that copy
# work. All of that is gone: Quarto generates the navbar from _quarto.yml and
# appends the footer from _includes/footer.html exactly as it does for the
# session pages, so there is nothing left to keep in sync.
#
# page-layout: custom suppresses Quarto's own <main> wrapper, the sidebar and
# the content column's max-width, which is what lets the hero and the bands run
# full-bleed. It also means the <main id="main"> below is the only <main> on the
# page, so the skip link still has a real target.
#
# pagetitle: rather than title:, plus title-block-style: none, so that <title>
# is set without generating a title block: the hero's own <h1> is then the
# page's only h1.
#
# The body is raw HTML in a ```{=html} block. This is layout - a two-column
# grid of fact pairs, card lists, logo bands - not prose, so fenced divs would
# stack four levels of ::: before the first word of copy without making
# anything clearer. The duplication was the problem here, and it is gone.
pagetitle: "Introduction to R for Biologists | Cambridge–Makerere Summer School 2026"
description: >-
  Introduction to R for Biologists — the R course taught at the
  Cambridge–Makerere Summer School 2026, Uganda Cancer Institute, Kampala,
  14–18 September 2026.
page-layout: custom
title-block-style: none
toc: false
---

<p class="lede">The materials are split into eight sessions, which do <b>not</b>

work through the materials in order and hopefully at least cover the first 7
sessions. The materials will remain available after the workshop, so you can
work through the later sessions in your own time.</p>
<p class="lede">Each session carries its own exercises with the answers folded away

<div>
<span class="eyebrow">About this course</span>
<h2>Why learn R?</h2>
<p class="lede"><b>R</b> is one of the leading programming languages in data
science, and the most widely used within the CRUK Cambridge Institute for
interacting with, analyzing and visualizing cancer biology data sets.</p>
<p>In this training course we aim to provide a friendly introduction to R,
pitched at a beginners level. We focus on manipulating tabular data and
visualising data, using a suite of packages known as the
<a href="https://www.tidyverse.org/">tidyverse</a> &mdash; in particular the
<em>dplyr</em> and <em>ggplot2</em> packages.</p>
<p>Working in scripts makes the steps of an analysis explicit: they can be
inspected by someone else, checked for errors, and re-run. An increasing
number of journals and funding agencies expect analyses to be reproducible,
so knowing R puts you ahead.</p>
</div>
<div>
<h3 class="rule-top">What you will cover</h3>
<ul class="topic-list">
<li><b>R and RStudio</b><span>Sessions 1&ndash;2</span></li>
<li><b>Data types and structures</b><span>Sessions 1&ndash;2</span></li>
<li><b>Reading and writing data</b><span>Session 3</span></li>
<li><b>Plotting with ggplot2</b><span>Sessions 4, 6&ndash;7</span></li>
<li><b>Wrangling with dplyr</b><span>Sessions 5&ndash;6</span></li>
<li><b>Tidy data and pivoting</b><span>Session 7</span></li>
<li><b>Reproducible reports</b><span>Session 8</span></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<div>
<span class="eyebrow">Before the first session</span>
<h2>Set your laptop up first</h2>
<p class="lede">You will need R and the tidyverse installed, and the workshop
data downloaded, before the first session. Installing R and its packages is
usually straightforward, but it can go wrong in ways that take time to fix
&mdash; so please work through the setup in advance and bring a laptop that
already works.</p>
<p class="lede">The data set is a single zip file. Download it, unzip it, and
keep the <code>Bioinformatics_Workshop</code> folder somewhere you can find
again &mdash; every session reads its files from the <code>data</code>
directory inside it.</p>
<p class="lede">If you get stuck, bring the error message with you and we will
sort it out before the practical starts.</p>
<div class="btn-row">
<a class="btn-brand btn-primary-brand" href="https://bioinformatics-core-shared-training.github.io/Cambridge_UCI_Summer_School_2026/prepare.html">Setup instructions</a>
<a class="btn-brand btn-ghost" href="Bioinformatics_Workshop.zip" download>Download the data (3&nbsp;MB)</a>
</div>
</div>
<div>
<h3>Going further</h3>
<ul class="linklist">
<li><a href="https://r4ds.hadley.nz/">R for Data Science<span class="meta">Book</span></a></li>
<li><a href="https://ggplot2-book.org/">ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis<span class="meta">Book</span></a></li>
<li><a href="https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/">Posit cheatsheets<span class="meta">PDF</span></a></li>
<li><a href="https://bioinformatics-core-shared-training.github.io/Cambridge_UCI_Summer_School_2026/">The Summer School<span class="meta">Site</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p style="margin-top:1.5rem">The <em>R for Data Science</em> book covers the
concepts introduced here in more depth, along with more advanced techniques
such as writing your own functions and iterating over vectors and lists. The
cheatsheets are well worth printing out and keeping to hand while you are
learning.</p>
